questions.prompt: What visual presentation does `.sheet` display by default on iOS?

options.text: A card overlay that slides up from the bottom of the screen.
options.explanation: Right. Sheets appear as card overlays sliding up from the bottom.

options.text: A full-screen modal covering all system status indicators.
options.explanation: FullScreenCover displays without margins, whereas sheet uses a card.

options.text: A centered modal dialog with two mandatory action buttons.
options.explanation: Centered popups with actions are alerts, not sheets.

options.text: A side navigation drawer sliding from the leading screen edge.
options.explanation: SwiftUI sheets slide up from the bottom edge on iOS.

questions.prompt: Which modifier displays a modal covering the entire display without card margins?

options.explanation: Sheets retain card margins and swipe gestures even when large.

options.text: The `.fullScreenCover(isPresented:)` modifier for full coverage.
options.explanation: Right. FullScreenCover covers the entire screen without card margins.

options.text: The `.navigationDestination(isPresented:)` modifier with push style.
options.explanation: NavigationDestination pushes views onto a navigation stack.

options.text: The `.confirmationDialog(isPresented:)` modifier on the root view.
options.explanation: ConfirmationDialog presents an action sheet, not a full-screen view.

options.explanation: Presentation detents configure vertical resting heights on iOS.

options.text: It locks the sheet position so users cannot dismiss it by swiping.
options.explanation: Disabling swipe dismissals is handled by interactiveDismissDisabled.

options.text: It specifies custom resting heights such as medium or large detents.
options.explanation: Right. Presentation detents allow sheets to rest at specific heights.

options.text: It controls screen rotation angles while the sheet is visible.
options.explanation: Orientation locking is managed through window orientation settings.

options.text: It supplies an unwrapped item, preventing nil crashes during dismissal.
options.explanation: Right. The content closure receives a valid unwrapped model object.

options.text: It runs the sheet presentation on an isolated background task.
options.explanation: View presentation and rendering always happen on the main thread.

options.text: It prevents users from taking screenshots of presented modal views.
options.explanation: SheetItem does not change window security or screenshot flags.

options.text: It caches rendered view hierarchies across multiple app launches.
options.explanation: SwiftUI views are lightweight structures and are not cached on disk.

options.text: The compiler throws a syntax error rejecting duplicate view modifiers.
options.explanation: The code compiles cleanly because view modifiers can be chained.

options.text: A presentation conflict causes one or both sheets to fail to open.
options.explanation: Right. Multiple sheets on the same view collide and fail to present.

options.text: SwiftUI displays both sheets at the same time in split view mode.
options.explanation: SwiftUI does not tile multiple sheets on top of each other.

options.text: The application crashes immediately with a memory leak exception.
options.explanation: It does not crash with a leak; presentation state simply gets ignored.

questions.prompt: Compare `.sheet(isPresented:)` and `.sheet(item:)`. Why is item-based presentation safer for model-driven modal views?
questions.modelAnswer: `.sheet(isPresented:)` accepts a Boolean binding. If the modal view relies on an optional model object, setting the model to nil during dismiss animation can crash the view. In contrast, `.sheet(item:)` binds to an optional Identifiable item. SwiftUI passes a non-optional unwrapped payload directly to the content closure. It guarantees the data remains valid throughout the dismissal animation.

rubric.criterion: Explains difference between Boolean isPresented and optional Identifiable item binding.
Notes unwrapped closure argument and prevention of nil crashes during dismissal animation.

questions.prompt: Explain the purpose of presentation detents in SwiftUI and how to configure them on iOS 16+.
questions.modelAnswer: Presentation detents control the resting heights of modal sheets on iOS 16 and later. By default, sheets expand to large size. Applying `.presentationDetents([.medium, .large])` allows users to drag sheets between half screen and full screen. Developers can also define custom fractions using `.fraction(0.4)` or fixed heights using `.height(250)`. You can also track and update the active detent using a state binding.

rubric.criterion: Identifies presentation detents as controlling resting sheet heights on iOS 16+.
Demonstrates usage of predefined cases like .medium and .large or custom fractions.

questions.prompt: Why does a presented sheet not display navigation bar titles from the presenting view, and how do you add one?
questions.modelAnswer: Modal sheets exist in a separate presentation window context outside the presenting view stack. They do not inherit the presenting view NavigationStack. To include navigation bar titles, toolbar buttons, or push links inside a sheet, you must wrap the sheet content in its own nested `NavigationStack`. This gives the modal its own independent title and toolbar controls.

rubric.criterion: Explains that sheets run in an isolated view hierarchy outside the parent navigation stack.
Explains wrapping the sheet content inside its own NavigationStack to add titles and toolbars.

questions.prompt: What is `.interactiveDismissDisabled` and when should an iOS developer use it?
questions.modelAnswer: `.interactiveDismissDisabled` is a view modifier that prevents users from dismissing a modal sheet with a downward swipe gesture. Developers use it when a sheet contains unsaved changes, active form input, or ongoing network tasks. Disabling swipe dismissal prevents accidental data loss. It forces the user to choose an explicit Cancel or Save button with confirmation.

rubric.criterion: Explains that the modifier disables the downward interactive swipe-to-dismiss gesture on sheets.
Mentions protecting unsaved form inputs, ongoing uploads, or forcing explicit button actions.

questions.prompt: Compare `alert` and `confirmationDialog` in SwiftUI. When should you pick each?
questions.modelAnswer: `alert` displays a centered dialog box on the screen. It is best for critical warnings, error messages, and simple two-button decisions. `confirmationDialog` slides up from the bottom on iPhone with a vertical list of actions. It is best for offering multiple choices related to a context, such as photo upload options or post actions. Confirmation dialogs automatically include a system Cancel button.

rubric.criterion: Describes alert as a centered dialog for critical errors, system warnings, and binary choices.
Describes confirmationDialog as a bottom action list for picking among multiple contextual options.
